name: Data Ethics and Governance
description:
This project week (11–15 January 2027) gives students the opportunity to collaborate with Local Contexts, under the leadership of experienced researchers, to address urgent challenges in the governance, sharing, and ethics linked to Indigenous data. Local Contexts (localcontext.org) is an Indigenous-led not for profit organization that works internationally to support Indigenous data sovereignty through an innovative system of data labelling. As an organization that delivers practical tools to support Indigenous aspirations for data governance, Local Contexts is seeking advice in developing a unique Local Contexts Dashboard to make more visible the vital connections and relationships between the varied users of the Local Contexts tools. These users include Indigenous communities, museums, libraries, archives and biodiversity data repositories and researchers. This project offers a rare chance for students and partners to engage in a shared space of theoretical and practical technical problem-solving with the goal of contributing to advancement in data ethics and Indigenous data sovereignty. 

The project adopts the format of a “data clinic,” which is an interactive problem-solving and teaching format designed to bridge theory and practice in the realm of data governance and ethics.  It creates an opportunity for both students and partners to enter a space of co-learning and problem-solving, and for students to make a real impact on embedding ethical principles around Indigenous data into database systems, guided by the Data Ethics team at the Chair of Philosophy and History of Science and Technology. The project also builds on the ground-breaking work done by the Ethical Data Initiative hosted at the TUM Think Tank. The project week will incorporate activities such as mini-lectures, expert talks, a data graphics workshop, and several Q&A sessions with a representative of the partner organisation. 

In sum: 
- Work with a leading Indigenous data sovereignty partners on real-world problems.
- Develop your talent as a next-generation researcher or practitioner with experience in data ethics. 
- Work intensively in a small group on problems with public interest stakes.
